title: Udall, Kansas · May 25, 1955
summary: A source-backed account of Udall's destruction, a regional forecast document and five separate historical records, with reported clocks, count differences and an unmatched county boundary kept visible.

records.basis: Kay County row at 22:00 CST, 8 miles and zero direct deaths or injuries. The separately named NWS Udall account and the five retained rows agree in county progression, F5 classification, aggregate 80 direct deaths and 273 direct injuries, and a maximum reported width of 1,320 yards. Their length fields total 56.4 miles versus 56 miles in the named account. The sources may share historical material. Each raw ID stays separate; no UTC, automatic join or surveyed track is inferred. Its ending [-97.15,37] does not match the next Sumner beginning [-97.25,37]; retain the discrepancy.

Sumner County row at 22:15 CST, 24.7 miles, 5 direct deaths and 3 direct injuries. The separately named NWS Udall account and the five retained rows agree in county progression, F5 classification, aggregate 80 direct deaths and 273 direct injuries, and a maximum reported width of 1,320 yards. Their length fields total 56.4 miles versus 56 miles in the named account. The sources may share historical material. Each raw ID stays separate; no UTC, automatic join or surveyed track is inferred. The unmatched Kay boundary remains unresolved. A coordinate match to the separate Blackwell control 10096417 is explicitly rejected.
alternatives: Rejected cross-event endpoint match to ncei:10096417, the separate Blackwell Kay control.

Matching neighboring endpoints support consistency only; continuation and narrative fields are blank.

media.title: A broad severe-weather forecast and its later caption
media.locator: NWS Wichita archive, Second Warning Issued link; complete 608 by 436 pixel image including the typewritten forecast and later archive caption. Issue, valid-period and caption broadcast labels are kept distinct.
media.account: The typewritten forecast describes possible tornadoes across a large city-defined region and requests immediate broadcast. Its heading has May 25 and an overtyped 4.36 PM issue label; the forecast period is 4.30 PM to 10 PM. The later archive caption supplies May 25, 1955, gives 4:36 P.M. and reports a broadcast by local media on the 5:00 news.
media.limits: The year and broadcast assertion belong to the later caption, not the typewritten body. No independent station record was obtained. Neither layer identifies a time zone, Blackwell broadcaster or resident who received it. The city-defined area is not converted into a polygon or explicit Blackwell warning. No tornado lead time or absolute event clock is derived.

place.reported: A broad region described through Dodge City, Amarillo, Wichita Falls, Ardmore and Wichita. This is attributed area wording, not a plotted warning polygon or explicit Blackwell receipt.
place.basis: Attributed document wording only; no registered location, warning polygon or camera point.

media.review: Agent visual inspection of the complete available original JPEG and its archive context on October 4, 2026 UTC. Typewritten text is distinguished from later caption additions. No human warning-receipt study, time calibration or spatial registration is claimed.

transformation.recipe: Exact original JPEG of an archival document preserved without crop, recoloring, resampling or caption removal. The existing photograph kind describes the document image, not storm footage.
transformation.alt: Typewritten severe-weather forecast with an overtyped issue time and immediate-broadcast request, above a later caption dated May 25, 1955.

reconstruction.limits: No registered camera, independently synchronized optical observation, calibrated UTC, geographic replay, historical wind field or continuous appearance interval is published. Source damage ratings, widths, endpoints and historical continuity interpretations do not supply those missing constraints.
